name: lodash-thisarg-removed-nodep
behavioral_change: lodash v4.0.0 removed the `thisArg` parameter from most methods. Calls such as `_.map(coll, callback, this)` and `_.forEach(coll, fn, this)` keep the same name and form, but the third argument no longer binds the callback, so `this` inside the callback is undefined.
downstream_effect: The downstream dependency-injection container has ten such calls in nodep.js whose callbacks read `this.dependencies` and `this.easyRegister`; after the upgrade each first read throws `TypeError: Cannot read property 'dependencies' of undefined`. The 18 failures name nodep.js but only with istanbul-instrumented positions (line 9, a license comment), so no usable line number is given for the ten edit sites spread over lines 183 to 501; lodash appears 108 times in stack frames, but thisArg and bind never appear.
reference_fix: The reference fix rewrites all ten calls in nodep.js from `_.map(coll, callback, this)` to `_.map(coll, _.bind(callback, this))`, following the Changelog example.
documented_in: The lodash Changelog for v4.0.0 (https://github.com/lodash/lodash/wiki/Changelog), Compatibility Warnings section, states that `thisArg` params were removed and can be replaced with `_.bind`, `Function#bind` or arrow functions, and includes a before/after code block (`_.map(objects, callback, context)` in 3.10.1 versus `_.map(objects, _.bind(callback, context))` in 4.0.0), which the reference fix follows verbatim.
failing_tests: $p.decorator should overwrite and inject old dependency
15 further failures of the same form, listed in pinned/STATE-NEW.log
